title: How do I tell if my AI-assisted game is “AI slop” or an actual game?
author: Baworistik
selftext:
I'm a solo dev and I used AI for some of the graphics and parts of the code. People talk about "AI slop" a lot, but I don't really understand where the line is.

What makes a game feel like slop to you? And how do I judge my own game honestly? (pls no "show it to others" - I don't really have anyone to playtest with)

comments.author: Braunb8888
comments.body: To me, AI slop is terrible looking generic UI, design that looks absurdly clean with zero personality, a game that’s barely a game. You can feel the soul of a videogame and some of these AI projects have absolutely no soul and yet they make money anyway which is terrible for AI game development in my opinion. If you’re showing who you are through the game, it’s not slop. If you’re showing me a generic ass call of duty copy you made in 2 hours, it’s slop.

replies.author: Novaworld7
replies.body: That's all subjective

replies.author: Braunb8888
replies.body: Yes and no. You can see ai art sometimes that looks fucking abysmal. That’s the slop look. It’s just like someone went “draw me this.” Then it does it and the person gave no notes or tweaks.

replies.author: zjgkkn
replies.body: Some people like it. It’s subjective. I’m trying to remove all non-AI content from my YouTube feed.

replies.author: Novaworld7
replies.body:
It is 100% subjective.

For example project zomboid / Minecraft to me looks like slop. Arma looks like slop. Wow looks like slop. 

They aren't slop, obviously but to me they look like slop.

replies.author: TheReservedList
replies.body: Then you have zero art direction talent or knowledge.

replies.author: Novaworld7
replies.body:
Why don't you show me 3 ui's that are uniquely different from one another where they don't have the same things. For example, grids, boxes, tables -_- it's all just subjective. For people to call it AI slop it's just dumb. 

I'm of the opinion that nearly all UI'S are just borderline identical with minor reskins. 

For example POE with the baubles and the vials to me is actually unique. 

But FFXIV / WOW / L2 / GW2 just identical slops.

replies.author: orbitsim
replies.body: Art is subjective woah

replies.author: dollarforthebusman
replies.body: This. Also, to add on, a lot of AI slop you'll notice is because they are just copying 1:1 something that has already been done, as you said with your COD example; there is no originality, and by removing the person from the creative process, there isn't any heart. A lot of popular play-together friend games that are popping off right now are made with AI, yet people still buy them in loads and don't complain about AI usage. Why? Because it's not slop. The devs actually made a new, refreshing concept, and didn't one shot the whole thing, they spent lots of time itterating to get THEIR vision across. The heart speaks so loudly that the AI software doesn't matter as much anymore.

comments.author: zjgkkn
comments.body:
I don’t quite understand this whole phenomenon; I used to think that this "slop police" was backed by AAA companies to make the barrier to entry for the market prohibitively high. But experienced artists and game designers see it differently. 

Personally, I just have specific triggers -- things like certain fonts, gold lettering on a dark green background, and other such obvious markers.

replies.author: Baworistik
replies.body: Yeah, me too. I also get something like an uncanny valley effect with some of projects, but still, it's hard to notice it in something you've been working on for several months and have gotten used to. + as someone said in another comment, it's quite subjective.

comments.author: gpubattle
comments.body:
Mostly just bugs and no constant art style.

I think they are the biggest signs. 

If its polished and the game plays good then it will do good regardless if AI helped. 

Plus a simplistic copy of something.

But even with AI to make a great game it will take time for any project.

replies.author: Baworistik
replies.body: I'm glad there are still opinions like that. Maybe it's a little bit of self-consolation, but I worked on my game nonstop for 2-3 months, and AI generated only a few images and models. All the other time I was working on the logic, story and other stuff, and I was worried it would all get buried under the "used AI" label.

replies.author: gpubattle
replies.body: I saw a chart where the games with an AI label on steam during the octoberfest actually did better then games without AI assistance so I think players don't care even though its a big in the dev community.

comments.author: PhotoDisastrous8275
comments.body: UH it looks good to me.. I think the art is very cool and if thats what it looked like in your head and you successfully made the pixels do what your head thought of, thats really all that matters.

comments.author: AfroJimbo
comments.body:
"Slop" to me is minimum input effort and minimum post-ai effort and then distributing it to the world. That's it, nothing more.

Did you spend a bunch of time designing and planning the inputs? Did you redo, or iterate from your first attempt to move towards something closer to your idea? Did you spend time editing and taking the AI assets into a post-production process of a large project?  

Not slop.

People are using the term to mean if they can detect if it's anything AI, it's "slop" which is an incredibly unproductive classification.

replies.author: InformationTop5376
replies.body: Yeah it’s an unfair classification as “slop” for even the littlest touch of AI, but with most things in life, it’s not about reality, but the optics and perception of something, however wrong or skewed that may be.

replies.author: J0rdian
replies.body: It's not just effort, you can spend hundreds of hours and the game can still look or play like AI Slop. At the end of the day it's just about making a good game.

replies.author: AfroJimbo
replies.body: But that's not "slop", that's just a shitty game.

replies.author: J0rdian
replies.body: Effort doesn't always change much, it really depends. It can't just be based on effort

replies.author: ensiferum888
replies.body: Slop is the eye of the beholder.

comments.author: TylerDurden1985
comments.body:
There's a vocal minority that are going to be against it no matter what - that's not your audience.  What you should care about are 

\- is it fun

\- is it unique

\- is there a compelling reason someone would spend money to play your game over another?

The thing about games is the product argues for itself.  If it's fun people will play it.  If it's not, or if it doesn't grab your attention, or warrant spending the limited free time the average gamer has, then they won't.  That's it.  Just make a good game.  Don't worry about the other stuff.

replies.author: kevin_whitley
replies.body:
This.

It all boils down to is it fun, does it seem reasonably different from existing titles (rather than a thin clone),  and does it have the right level of polish.

If you try to one-shot a concept based on something vague like "I want a viral game that'll sell loads of copies", it'll create uber-slop, copying existing models/titles with very thin variation.  You'll be judged (rightly so).  
  
So basically don't do that.

comments.author: TopTippityTop
comments.body:
1. Does it look like AI? (Warm wash, artifacts, lack of visual identity on the overall game and content, generic concepts, overly detailed insignificant areas, common AI fonts, generic layouts and ideas, lack of clear focus, devoid of personality and intent)
2. Is it well designed? Well balanced? Fun? Does it have that human thought behind how systems mesh together (AI tends to fumble game design quite a lot)
3. Does it have more features, mechanics and other things than necessary because it's now easy to do?

replies.author: Fit_Emergency_9872
replies.body: Especially 1

comments.author: alanbdee
comments.body:
It's really a problem of; is your game slop. If you put in the time. Tested it. It's bug free. It may be labeled as slop but it's not. You have to understand that there's a bunch of people out there trying to one-shot a game. A shotgun approach if you will. Hoping to get that next Find a Needle type simple game. 

If you're doing one game, put a lot of time into it. Then its not AI slop.

replies.author: kevin_whitley
replies.body:
100%.

AI certainly doesn't mean slop, but one-shotting \*does\* certainly tend to create it.  Weirdly I find both novices (non-technical) and seasoned devs alike try to one-shot.   It's like "if I can give it enough requirements it'll make it perfect"... or maybe i just need the right model, or the right skills, or the right orchestration loop...

Everyone finds their own flavor, but I've found WAY better results iteratively growing a product/idea, bit by bit just like you'd build it yourself.  It just executes on those ideas/steps 1,000,000x faster than you would.  Still takes a lot of human time and validation/steering along the way, but if you try to fully cut that step, slop risk is high.

comments.body: Who cares, it looks shit

Anything that is bad = slop.   
anything made with ai that is bad more specifically = AI slop.

It just seems poorly put together. But not to an extreme that would bother me, or make my say “slop”

gossip goblin is not slop.

the rest is a spectrum between those points

comments.author: eradias
comments.body:
Have you play tested it? Like have YOU actually tried it end to end? 

AI slop becomes evident mostly in the game play when it becomes total shit after the initial 2 min shine

comments.author: JorgitoEstrella
comments.body: Compare it to the top 10 games in its niche, if its better than most of them then its a good game if it's worse than all of them then its slop.

comments.author: TorthOrc
comments.body:
Start with your mechanics for your game and the different game loops it will go through. 

Remove all your sprites and play the game with boxes first.   
You need to work out if your game flows.

What the game feels like as you are playing it without any graphics at all.

Certain things may sound like fun, but if a player finds they aren’t enjoying the game loops themselves then it needs work. 

Once you have that down, then you can start building on top of that. 

When push comes to shove, how a game looks will mean nothing if the gameplay itself isn’t satisfying. 

Good luck!  
You’ve got this!

There is nothing wrong with using ai to help express yourself and be creative. 

Give it time and work it slow from the ground up. 

Slop is just a word for bad food.   
Anyone can learn to be a good cook.

comments.author: Key-Trainer6854
comments.body:
I feel like a lot of pre 2023 indie games would have been labeled "AI slop" even though no AI was used. Nowadays the terms just seems to refer to low quality, low effort, cashgrab games regardless of how much AI was used the process.

Also if you have little experience developing games then you are likely to produce slop whether you want it or not.

replies.author: drahgon
replies.body: I doubt it because it’s not about being low quality. It’s about low effort more than anything even if your quality of your graphics are low it feels unique and you put in your real hard work into it. It’s still gonna not feel like slop

replies.body: They were called Asset Flips before no?

replies.body: Exactly

comments.author: Pljeskavac
comments.body:
"AI slop" is a spectrum that means different things to different people. Generally speaking, as many pointed out in the comments, it means little effort, no distinction or uniqueness, that screams "no soul".

>*pls no "show it to others" - I don't really have anyone to playtest with*

Sorry to break it to you, but without this component, you may end up having a game but you'll probably never have a product. Without having the step that turns your game into a product that someone would be willing to buy, whether or not your game is classified as "AI slop" won't matter to your potential success.

My advice would be the following

1 - Get the game to a point you're satisfied with, that gives you the creator a good and enjoyable experience. Iterate and polish until you're happy with a working prototype (couple of levels, act one of a story w/e makes sense in the context of your game). Some checks you can do on your own:

   * Consistency: Do all your assets share pixel scale, palette, lighting and line weight?
   * Artifacts: Look for warped details, garbled symbols, things that don’t make physical sense
   * Authorship: What’s the one thing in this game that only you would have made? If you can’t name it, that’s the problem, not the AI
   * Core loop: Is there a clear thing the player does that’s fun on its own, or is it a pile of features?

2 - Try engaging your friends and family to help you out in play testing your game (if you can't get your friends and family engaged, how do you expect to engage potential customers?). Iterate and polish until again you're satisfied where your project is at.

3 - Define your targeted customer.

What is your game supposed to do?

Is it a game designed to tell a captivating story? Is it a competitive type where people will compete with one another, chasing high scores on a global leaderbord? Is it a challenge that requires you to use your noggin extensively, or a cozy simulator made for a dad of 2 after a long day of work, who wants to use their limited time to relax?

Once you have your targeted customer in mind, penetrate the spaces you could find them, promote your game there and build a community around it. If your prototype is good and scratches a certain itch, people would be more than willing to help you out. Build on the communities feedback, fix bugs that are inevitably going to show up.

Successfully completing 1-3 will rule out the chances of your game being called "AI slop".

Best of luck! :)

comments.author: Kooky-Anything4450
comments.body: Don't worry about it, if it's a game that you like playing and be happy paying for release it.

comments.author: drahgon
comments.body: Slop is in the eye of the beholder, but if you put enough time in and take pride in the game, you’re making even if you use AI, you probably won’t end up with slop.

comments.author: TalkingHeadsVideo
comments.body: AI Slop is just whatever a cult member decides is slop.  In another sub, I saw one anti-AI activist rant about slop on a game that didn't use AI. He kept doubling down, eventually reduced to. "It looks like AI." as his argument.

comments.author: d1knight
comments.body: You already know whether your game is slop or not. The real question is how to hide the slop from players. The answer is you can’t.

comments.author: sillyandstrange
comments.body: Depends on who you talk to.

comments.author: Felfedezni
comments.body: Is it fun and good? Not slop.

comments.author: alaershov
comments.body:
There's no line, and a lot of heated discussion, but here's my take.

If you replace your creativity with AI, don't care about the game and just want to make a quick buck, it's slop.

If you have a creative vision, and use AI to help implement your game, to ensure the best possible quality, and perfect the experience you want to deliver, it's your game.

I'm not touching the ethics and other aspects of AI as a technology here, it's a whole other topic.

comments.author: UnironicallyDel
comments.body: the line is: dont use ai. Is what I would say if a majority of video games didnt have NPCs which are technically ai but not gen ai.

comments.author: twendah
comments.body: Thats not AI assisted. Thats pure slob

comments.author: Ok_Feedback4200
comments.body:
From design standpoint - if you use image generators and use their output as final - it's auto slop... Doesn't matter what's it made for or where it's used. But.. I'd say that if you use AI to enhance your workflow and still have full control of your assets, then I don't see a reason to call it slop. Because an effort was made, workflow was thoughtout, all creative controls and decisions remain in our hands... Unlike with image generators where you are always at the mercy of what that engine will produce for you.

As far as coding goes... Most of real programmers in actual big companies don't write code anymore. Do they produce slop then? I don't think so..

If you are a solo dev and not using AI, there's simply no way to produce a good or new game without spending many years on it. Why should that remain the default and the 'correct' way to produce games? If you have full control of your game, if you planned everything in it, but then let the AI figure out how the code needs to work.. Who cares? Also, I'm quite sure that if most AAA companies started using proper AI workflows, we'd atleast get more finished games with less bugs in them on release. We are past the point where AI is a better coder than humans. Input still matters though, a lot...

comments.author: Agile_Branch_8743
comments.body: The main question for me is: have you put thought and care about the gameplay and art's design and direction? Did you gradually build on your concept? Or did you prompt AI to make you an X type game? I think that's the main difference. You can't control people's reaction, though. For me, your screenshot doesn't look like AI slop.

comments.author: Puzzleheaded_Bug595
comments.body:
For some people, any game that uses AI is automatically "AI slop."

For me, AI slop is when it's obvious that the developer doesn't really understand game design, the mechanics have clear flaws, and the generated content hasn't even been properly reviewed or refined.I think the real problem isn't AI itself, but the lack of care and effort put into the final product.And if we're going to use the term "AI slop," we should probably also have "Human slop." People have been making terrible games without AI for decades.

comments.author: shoukachidev
comments.body:
For me personally it is when you can see and feel that there is no vision behind it. You can see they didnt use AI as a tool, but rather as the brain.   
Also: When the game is just not fun to play

comments.author: NoBackupDev
comments.body: Play the game. If you find it fun and it makes you want to play more, its not slop.

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
If others agree...
To many people blinded by there own hubris.

comments.author: PsykopompM
comments.body: Do you know how to code? Did you look at the code that the AI made? Did you understand what you were looking at? Did you confirm that it was coded correctly? If the answer to all of these are "yes", then it's not vibe coded/slop.

comments.author: Arzlynd
comments.body: Show it to others.  You already seem to know the answer...Find a Discord about AI game making and find people willing to try it.  The internet is a vast place.

comments.author: linkandluke
comments.body: The community will tell you.

comments.author: GlobalCurry
comments.body: Do you do the level design and define the game mechanics and rules? I think those are what differentiate "ai slop" from a good game. Like you can have ai build out the mechanics and systems and rules of your game but it's awful at making good levels or making actually interesting gameplay on its own.
